title: Week in Orbit
summary: This week, the space industry is navigating a mix of budgetary constraints and strategic partnerships, with a notable focus on resilience and safety. Meanwhile, the hypersonic glide-vehicle program continues to stumble, raising questions about readiness.

themes.title: Budgetary Tightrope Walk
themes.body: House appropriators have approved a spending bill that keeps NASA's budget flat, while the FY27 budget markup adds $1.4 billion to space resilience. This juxtaposition highlights the ongoing struggle to balance innovation with fiscal responsibility.

themes.title: Mergers and Acquisitions Buzz
themes.body: Iridium's acquisition of Aireon signals a strategic move to bolster aviation safety services, while Palantir's $480 million extension on the TITAN program reflects the growing importance of data in defense. Expect more consolidation as companies seek to enhance their capabilities.

themes.title: Hypersonic Hurdles Persist
themes.body: For the third consecutive quarter, the hypersonic glide-vehicle test has slipped, casting doubt on the program's timeline and efficacy. This ongoing delay underscores the complexities of developing cutting-edge military technologies.

themes.title: Space Partnerships Evolving
themes.body: Anduril and L3Harris are teaming up on a tactical SDA constellation bid, demonstrating a trend towards collaboration in the defense sector. As the landscape shifts, expect more alliances to form in pursuit of advanced capabilities.
